The L Component

Models for Immature Mosquito Ecology

Source: vignettes/L-interface.Rmd
L-interface.Rmd

The L component models aquatic mosquito ecology across larval habitats. This vignette describes its interfaces and the methods implemented by an L module (Figure 1). Each L module uses the dynamical term, eta or \(\eta\), the number of eggs laid in the habitat each day

eta <- xds_obj$terms$eta[[s]]

Each module defines a function F_emerge (or \(F_\alpha\)) to compute the number of emergent adults, \(\alpha\). Development from eggs to adults is described by a dynamical system. The following describes the structure of the L component.

Figure 1 - A diagram of the L Component in context. The L component is linked to adult mosquito ecology through egg laying and emergence. A function, F_eggs returns the number of eggs laid by adult mosquitoes in each patch, denoted by \(G\). The egg-distribution matrix \(U\) allocates eggs among habitats, so each habitat gets \(\eta\) eggs per day. The L module then computes its dynamics and the emergence rate \(\alpha\) in each habitat. The emergence interface aggregates \(\alpha\), using the habitat membership matrix, into the patch-specific adult emergence rate \(\Lambda\).

Module methods

Most methods dispatch on the class of xds_obj$L_obj[[s]], where s is the vector-species index. The setup generic instead dispatches on the supplied module name; the skill-set generic accepts either a model or a module name. Model-specific methods use s consistently. There is no fixed number of methods that every module must implement: implement the dynamics method that matches the model and the outputs and setup methods needed by its interfaces.

Dynamics

Implement one of the following:

  • dLdt.Lname for a continuous-time model. It receives t, the dependent-variable vector y, xds_obj, and s, and returns derivatives in the same order as the model’s state variables.
  • Update_Lt.Lname for a discrete-time model. It receives the same arguments and returns the updated state variables in state-variable order.

The functions are used by the continuous-time or discrete-time solver pathways, respectively.

Derivative titles use “Compute the derivatives for module (L)”. Begin descriptions “Compute the derivatives for the module module:” and show the implemented equations immediately below. Inherit the module NULL anchor’s state, input-term, parameter, and ODE or Dynamics sections, plus relevant model-specific sections. Preserve existing section names: basicL uses Dynamical Term and ODE; stages uses Egg Laying, Mean Crowding, and Dynamics. Put dispatch on xds_obj$L_obj[[s]] in the generic note.

Return “a [numeric] vector of derivatives in the module’s state-variable order”, with the actual length. Document block order and the egg-input storage path in @note. basicL returns L in habitat order, with length nHabitats; stages returns E, L1, L2, L3, L4, and P blocks, each in habitat order, with total length 6 * nHabitats. The trivialL method retains its empty-vector description and return value.

Update titles use “Update states for module (L)”. Begin descriptions “Update the state variables for the module module:” and show the updating equations in \deqn{} immediately below. Inherit the same NULL-anchor sections as the derivative method, replacing ODE with DTS. For basicL, retain State Variables, Dynamical Term, Parameters, Emergence, and Regulation as well. Document dispatch in the generic note, and habitat ordering and egg-input storage in the method note. Return “a [numeric] vector of updated states in the module’s state-variable order, with length nHabitats”. The trivialL method remains an empty-vector no-op; stages has no discrete-time update method.

State-variable extraction

The number of state values is generally based on nHabitats, not nPatches. The membership vector associates each habitat with a patch.

State-variable getters primarily serve solver evaluations that need variables by name; users rarely call them directly. Follow the shared getter conventions: use “Get the state variables for module (L)”, describe extraction from y for model solving, put index storage in @note, and return a named list of state variables and module-specific derived quantities. Keep this separate from parsing solver-output matrices.

Aquatic Bionomics

Two methods update bionomic parameter values before the dynamics are computed.

  • LBionomics.Lname – evaluates the baseline bionomic parameter functions for the current time and resets the effect sizes to 1.

For every parameter x configured as a port, LBionomics stores the baseline in x_t and resets es_x to 1. LEffectSizes then sets x = x_t * es_x. Parameters without ports are stored directly as x and are not modified by effect sizes. In particular, stages has no bionomic parameter ports: its constructor and parameter changer store direct values, and its bionomics and effect-size methods leave them unchanged.

  • LEffectSizes.Lname – applies vector control effect sizes to the bionomic parameters set by LBionomics.

Both methods receive t, y, xds_obj, and s, and return the updated xds_obj.

Retain the titles “Mosquito bionomics for module (L)” and “Apply effect sizes for module (L)”. Inherit the module NULL anchor’s Parameters section and link the two methods reciprocally and to the module. For basicL, distinguish baseline evaluation and effect-size resets from realization of psi, phi, xi, and theta; put the stored fields and per-habitat assignments in @note. For stages, retain the descriptions that both methods leave directly stored parameters unchanged. Document dispatch on xds_obj$L_obj[[s]] in the generic notes.

Egg input and emergence output

The egg-laying interface computes patch-level adult egg production \(G\) using F_eggs, then distributes eggs to aquatic habitats. If \(O\) is the habitat-by-patch egg-laying matrix, \(Q\) is the availability of modeled habitats in each patch, and \(Q_{\mathrm{all}}\) is total egg-laying availability, the habitat-level input is

\[ \eta = O\left(G \circ \frac{Q}{Q_{\mathrm{all}}}\right), \]

where \(\circ\) denotes element-wise multiplication. Thus, \(\eta\) has one value per habitat and is supplied to the L dynamics.

F_emerge.Lname returns the adult emergence quantity \(\alpha\), with one value per habitat. It is a rate for a continuous-time model and a number for a discrete-time model. The emergence interface aggregates habitat emergence by patch using the habitat membership matrix \(N\):

\[ \Lambda = N\alpha. \]

Use “Compute adult mosquito emergence for module (L)” for method titles; the generic omits “for module”. Use the short description “Return adult female mosquito emergence per habitat.” Methods inherit @inheritSection module Emergence from their module NULL anchor, where the formula and biological details belong. Return “a [numeric] vector of length nHabitats” and link to the module and Emergence. Document dispatch on xds_obj$L_obj[[s]] in the generic note. Flag formula discrepancies separately: F_emerge.stages currently returns psi_P*P/2, while its anchor gives psi_P*P.

Dynamical parameter accessors

get_psi, get_phi, get_xi, and get_theta return the stored realized maturation rate, density-independent mortality rate, delayed maturation parameter, and slope of density-dependent mortality, respectively, per habitat. They do not evaluate ports or apply effect sizes. Refresh port-backed values through bionomics and effect-size application before reading them. Currently, only basicL implements these accessor methods.

Retain the titles “Get the parameter for module (L)”, using the parameter’s full name; generic titles omit “for module”. Use short stored-realized-value descriptions, inherit the module NULL anchor’s Parameters section, and return “a [numeric] vector of length nHabitats”. Put dispatch on xds_obj$L_obj[[s]] and the absence of port evaluation or effect-size application in the generic note. Link methods to their module and corresponding change_psi, change_phi, change_xi, or change_theta.

Model object and parameters

make_L_obj_Lname creates the module-specific L object, and setup_L_obj.Lname attaches it to the full model at xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]. The setup method also receives the habitat-to-patch membership vector and initializes shared habitat interfaces.

  • get_L_pars.Lname returns the module’s parameters as a named list.
  • change_L_pars.Lname changes supported parameter values using the named list options.

The shared change_psi, change_phi, change_xi, and change_theta helpers change individual static basicL parameters. Each accepts a numeric scalar, repeated across habitats, or values of length nHabitats. Invalid types or lengths cause an error. For parameter x, the helper sets xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]$x; when x_obj is present, it also sets x_t and x_obj$x. It leaves the port class and es_x unchanged and does not evaluate ports or apply effect sizes. It returns the updated model object. These ordinary functions do not dispatch on the module or port class; they are not a way to reconfigure a dynamic port.

Retain the “Change the parameter (L)” titles, using the full parameter name. Describe the static basicL scope, inherit its Parameters section, document scalar/per-habitat inputs, and put storage and update mechanics in @note. Keep reciprocal links to the corresponding parameter getters.

Initial values

make_L_inits_Lname returns a named list of default initial values for all state variables. setup_L_inits.Lname stores the values at xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]$inits; get_L_inits and change_L_inits.Lname inspect and update them.

get_L_inits is an ordinary function, not an S3 generic. It returns the selected species’ stored inits field directly: a named list of initial values, an empty list for trivialL after setup, or NULL if absent. Keep storage in a documentation note and link to setup/change functions; follow the shared getter wording in the documentation conventions.

Title the constructor “Make initial values for module (L)” and describe it as “Create a named list of initial values for the module module. Values in options override the defaults.” Its return description is “a named [list] of initial values”. Preserve model-specific explanations. Document numeric scalar expansion to nHabitats and the required length for non-scalar initial values. The constructor, setup method, and change method each link to the other two in @seealso, following the shared documentation conventions.

Use “Set up initial values for module (L)” as the setup-method title. Describe calling the initial-value constructor and options overrides. Put storage at xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]$inits in @note, and return “an xds model object”. Trivial methods describe their actual behavior instead of claiming to call a constructor.

Title initial-value changers “Change initial values for module (L)”. Use “Change initial values named in options for the module module, leaving other values unchanged.” Preserve supported-value explanations, put storage explanations in @note, and return “an xds model object”. Keep reciprocal constructor/setup links, and report implementation discrepancies separately during documentation alignment.

Variable indices

setup_L_ix.Lname assigns indices to the module’s state variables; get_L_ix retrieves the stored indices.

get_L_ix(xds_obj, s = 1) is an ordinary function, not an S3 generic. It returns the module’s stored ix field directly: a named list of variable indices, an empty list if stored, or NULL if absent. Document storage in @note, link to setup_L_ix, and follow the shared index-getter conventions.

Title indexing methods “Set up variable indices for module (L)”. Describe consecutive allocation after xds_obj$max_ix, list block order and lengths, and return “an xds model object”. Put storage at xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]$ix and the updated maximum in @note. Follow the shared indexing conventions; trivial methods describe their actual no-op behavior.

Parsing outputs

get_L_orbits(xds_obj, s = 1) retrieves saved, parsed orbits (trajectories) after solving for L for the selected species. It returns a list of module-specific outputs with time added from xds_obj$outputs$time. It reads xds_obj$outputs$orbits$L[[s]]; it does not parse outputs or modify the model. Use the title “Get orbits (L)” and the shared orbit-getter conventions.

  • parse_L_orbits.Lname extracts named states and any model-specific derived quantities from the solver output matrix.

Follow the shared output-parser conventions: use “Parse outputs for module (L)”, describe extraction from outputs into a named list, and use “a [list]” for returns. Put index storage at xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]$ix in a method note, and describe any derived quantities. Parsers process trajectories after solving and return results without modifying the model object; the output-processing pipeline stores them at xds_obj$outputs$orbits$L[[s]].

Checks and skill set

check_L.Lname provides a hook for module-specific consistency checks before solving. Existing methods currently return the model unchanged and perform no checks.

get_skillset_L.Lname returns the module’s capabilities and compatibilities as a list, which setup stores on the module object. A module without Update_Lt.Lname must include dts = FALSE.

Non-trivial modules report psi_is_port, phi_is_port, xi_is_port, and theta_is_port. Each flag is TRUE for a parameter implemented as a port and FALSE for a direct or absent parameter. All four are TRUE for basicL and FALSE for stages.

The basicL example

The basicL module tracks larval density \(L\) in each aquatic habitat. It uses the habitat-level egg input \(\eta\), maturation rate \(\psi\), crowding-dependent maturation parameter \(\xi\), density-independent mortality rate \(\phi\), and density-dependent mortality parameter \(\theta\). Its continuous-time equation is

\[ \frac{dL}{dt} = \eta - \left(\psi e^{-\xi L} + \phi + \theta L\right)L. \]

The corresponding habitat-level adult emergence rate is

\[ \alpha = \psi e^{-\xi L}L. \]

Setting \(\xi=0\) recovers the model described by Smith et al. (2013). basicL also implements Update_Lt.basicL. Its steady-state method, steady_state_L.basicL, delegates to steady_state_L_basicL, which selects the differential-equation or discrete-time calculation.

Solving and visualization

steady_state_L.Lname is an optional method for computing a model’s steady state from habitat-level egg input \(\eta\). get_L_orbits retrieves the parsed L output from a solved xds object. The shared xds_plot_L and xds_lines_L functions plot aquatic mosquito population density; modules do not need to implement L-specific plotting generics.

Steady-state method titles use “Compute steady states for module (L)”, apart from explicitly retained titles. Descriptions identify the daily egg input eta and supported equation system; return documentation names the states in the returned list. The generic dispatches on xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]. For basicL, the second-stage generic dispatches on xds_obj$xds to select xde or dts; both return a list containing L. The stages method implements the differential-equation calculation and returns E, L1, L2, L3, L4, and P. These functions return values without storing them on the model object.

For details on a specific model, see its module documentation and the relevant literature. The basicL equations are based on Smith et al. (2013), listed in the references below.

Documentation conventions

Follow the shared function order in module and component files and in guide implementation sections. Keep functions with their documentation and preserve file-level review/TODO notes at the top.

Follow the shared documentation conventions for titles, equations, descriptions, notes, return values, and punctuation. Use L as the component tag. Bionomics and effect-size method titles are “Mosquito bionomics for module (L)” and “Apply effect sizes for module (L)”.

Document derivative equations and discrete-time updating equations separately, matching the implemented formulas and returned state ordering. State whether emergence is a continuous-time rate or a discrete-time number, and distinguish habitat-level quantities from patch-level quantities.

Constructors use “Make a module object for module (L)” as their title. Describe parameter initialization and options overrides, and identify the parameter getter and changer. The constructor, get_L_pars.Lname, and change_L_pars.Lname each link to the other two in @seealso. Document any differences in the parameters those functions support.

Parameter-changer titles use “Change parameters for module (L)”. Start the description with “Change parameter values named in options for the module module, leaving other values unchanged.” Describe which baseline fields are updated, whether bionomics and effect sizes are refreshed immediately, and when changes take effect. After parameter or port changes, call LBionomics(0, y, xds_obj, s) using the flattened initial state y; do not call LEffectSizes from the changer. Return an xds model object.

Setup documentation

Use the title “Set up the module object for module (L)” and start the description with “Set up a/an module module object for the L component and the relevant vector species.”

List the constructor using nHabitats and options, the skill set, and initial-value setup in implementation order. Describe the habitat-interface step as “Initialize habitat search weights using [setup_habitat_search_weights.setup].” End with “Return the updated xds model object.”

In roxygen, the bracketed helper name is a link; qualify it with ramp.xds:: in ramp.library. Keep object storage, class assignments, and dispatch mechanics in @note. Setup methods return an xds model object, not just the component list.
